I farm small land, and I have to keep the plan simple, steady, and manageable with two people in the house. I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best, it fits my well irrigation, and it gives me grain in both seasons. I will keep a smaller piece in cotton because I already grow it and I do not want to put all my land into one pattern. Since I have farmed for 40 years and do not have much labor to spare, I will choose inputs that are dependable rather than complicated. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen for a stable stand, add phosphorus for rooting, and a moderate amount of potassium. I will irrigate several times because wheat in Hebei needs water at key stages. After wheat, I will plant hybrid maize on the same land because it gives stronger yield, and I will fertilize it a bit heavier on nitrogen than wheat. Cotton takes longer and needs more watching, so I will keep it on a smaller area, use improved seed, fertilize it steadily, irrigate a few times from the well, and spray more often than grain crops because insects are usually a bigger issue there. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical on my small farm and easier to manage across the year.
